title: Encode composite keys for local comparisons
brief: RowConverter is a comparison representation with converter-specific ordering, not a durable wire format. Decoding preserves values but hydrates dictionaries.

choices.tradeoff: Associate rows with the same converter; configure descending/null placement per field.

choices.choose_when: Only sorted row positions are needed
choices.tradeoff: Avoid managing your own encoded-row lifecycle.
Keep execution and optimization in the engine.

choices.choose_when: Persistence or cross-process compatibility is required
choices.tradeoff: Define a format/schema compatibility policy; bytes alone do not define durable identity.

claims.statement: RowConverter::new takes ordered SortFields. convert_columns takes &[ArrayRef] and returns Rows; convert_rows returns Vec<ArrayRef>, not a reconstructed schema.
Upstream requires compared rows to come from the same converter. Rows exposes borrowed Row views; OwnedRow owns row bytes. Row encoding may change across releases.

Dictionary inputs are hydrated for row encoding. The Int8/Utf8 probe decodes to Utf8, not Dictionary<Int8,Utf8>; exact dictionary assignments require preserving separate representation information or choosing another format.
SortOptions controls null placement and direction. Do not infer application collation, canonical equality or stable float encoding from lexicographic byte comparison.

implementation: Keep converter configuration associated with rows.
Validate decoded physical types and schema separately from value equality.
Use a specified interchange format when output must outlive the local comparison contract.
unknowns: Float/nested/extension domain equivalence and cross-release serialization are not qualified.
The IPC round trip preserves dictionary type, keys and values in one pinned process/profile; it does not certify arbitrary reader/writer version pairs.
